title: The Physician's Son: Mecca, the Commission, and the Yacht Named for a Daughter
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Mecca, birth in the royal physician's house
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A son is born to Muhammad Khashoggi, an ethnic Turk who serves as personal physician to King Abdul Aziz Al Saud, and to Samiha Ahmed. The household sits close to the court and closer still to the body of the man who made the kingdom. The boy learns early what the rest of his life will monetize: that a sovereign's ear is a finite resource, and that whoever the sovereign permits near him holds something no factory can manufacture. This ground already belongs to pilgrims walking toward the Kaaba. Khashoggi is born inside it.
suggested_refs: The Masjid al-Haram district of Mecca, nearest fixed landmark to an unrecorded birth address

stops.name: Alexandria, Victoria College
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the source gives the school but no year at all
stops.campa: He is sent to Victoria College in Alexandria, the Anglophone school that turns out the region's ruling class: King Hussein of Jordan sits in its rooms, and Omar Sharif. The pupils arrive as Libyans, Egyptians, Palestinians, Saudis and Jordanians, and leave speaking one another's money. Khashoggi's father pays for an English education and receives a broker. The school is attested and the alumni roster is confirmed on the college's own record; the year of enrollment is placement, not testimony, and is carried at low confidence.
suggested_refs: Victoria College on El Iqbal Street, Alexandria

stops.name: Alexandria, the towel deal
stops.date_confidence: tradition; undated anecdote with no source year
stops.campa: The story the family tells, and that he never corrects: a Libyan classmate's father wants towels, an Egyptian classmate's father makes them, and the schoolboy standing between them takes a fee for introducing two men who would otherwise never meet. Roughly a thousand dollars changes hands. He never touches a towel. What he sells is the introduction, and the fee is paid for that alone. He is a teenager in an Alexandria classroom, and the shape of every deal he will make for the next fifty years is already fixed.
suggested_refs: The origin anecdote of the first commission, told in every profile and dated in none

stops.name: Chico, California State University
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; no year and no order in the source
stops.campa: He crosses to California and enrolls at Chico State, in the rice country of the Sacramento Valley, a long way from Mecca and further still from the Alexandria corniche. The American degree is what wealthy Gulf families are buying that decade, a certificate of modernity to hang beside the agency contracts. The source lists Chico, Ohio State and Stanford as a bare series, in no stated order and with no dates attached; the sequence laid out across these stops is arrangement, and is flagged as such.
suggested_refs: The Chico State campus, first of three American universities he leaves without a degree

stops.name: Columbus, Ohio State University
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; no year and no order in the source
stops.campa: Columbus is the second American campus in a list of three that nobody puts in order. He studies briefly and moves on. He enters the institution and takes what is transferable from it, the names and the addresses, then leaves before it can ask anything of him in return. A university wants four years and a thesis. What Khashoggi wants from it is the corridor, and the corridor is open in the first semester, which is roughly how long he stays anywhere that issues a diploma.
suggested_refs: Ohio State University, the American campus most often dropped from retellings of his education

stops.name: Palo Alto, Stanford and the Kenworth trucks
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the truck deal is undated tradition
stops.campa: At Stanford he leaves college altogether without a degree. His father sends money for a car; he buys a fleet of Kenworth trucks instead and leases them to a construction firm, clearing two hundred and fifty thousand dollars and, with it, the Kenworth agency for Saudi Arabia. The trucks are leased and not resold: he keeps the asset and sells the use of it, which is the towel deal again with heavier equipment. He is twenty, and he holds the Kenworth agency for an entire country before he holds a degree from anywhere.
suggested_refs: The Kenworth agency for Saudi Arabia, first of the agency contracts

stops.name: Jeddah, the port of the arrangement
stops.date_confidence: inferred from the general account of his Saudi base
stops.campa: Jeddah becomes the port of the arrangement. Western manufacturers cannot sell into the kingdom without a Saudi agent of record, and the kingdom is about to spend oil money on everything a country can buy: trucks, cement, airfields, radar, hospitals. Khashoggi collects the agencies one by one and takes his percentage off the top of contracts he neither builds nor delivers. The Red Sea port that for centuries handled pilgrims bound for Mecca now handles the paperwork of the largest construction program on earth.
stops.quote: A quoi servent donc un avocat, un medecin ?
stops.quote_source: Khashoggi defending the middleman's fee by analogy to professional fees, Le Point interview of 1977, reproduced in La Revue du Liban et de l'Orient arabe, 19 February 1977, p. 33; spoken two decades after this stop
suggested_refs: Jeddah as agency capital of the Saudi construction boom

stops.name: Riyadh, the court and the first marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the marriage year; the Riyadh placement is inferred
stops.campa: In Riyadh he works the court itself, the princes and the ministries, until foreign firms understand that a Saudi contract runs through him or does not run. His father's proximity to Abdul Aziz becomes his own proximity to Abdul Aziz's sons. He marries Sandra Daly, a British woman who converts to Islam and takes the name Soraya; she bears a daughter, Nabila, and four sons. The daughter's name will be painted on a hull two decades later and become the most photographed object he ever owns.
suggested_refs: The Saudi royal court at Riyadh, the relationship his father's medical bag opened

stops.name: Geneva, Triad founded for three brothers
stops.date_confidence: contested; the source says only 'the early 1960s' and names no place
stops.campa: Triad International Holding Company is founded and named for three brothers: Adnan, Essam and Adil. It will grow into hotels, oil refineries, banks, computer manufacturing, gold mines and an American basketball franchise across five continents. Where it was founded is not settled. This stop places it in Geneva; the same research elsewhere names Saudi Arabia and Liechtenstein; the source consulted specifies no location at all and no year beyond the early nineteen sixties. The contradiction is left standing.
suggested_refs: Triad Holding Corporation, the vehicle through which every later holding is recorded

stops.name: Sana'a, arms to Stirling's operation in Yemen
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the source misnames the conflict
stops.campa: He supplies weapons to David Stirling's covert operation in Yemen, the founder of the Special Air Service running mercenaries on the royalist side against Egyptian-backed republicans. The conflict is habitually misnamed in the sources as the Aden Emergency, which was the anti-British insurgency of the NLF and FLOSY in the south; Stirling's men fought in the north, in the civil war of 1962 to 1970. The two wars are distinct and are separated here. This is the first time Khashoggi's commissions are paid in something that kills.
suggested_refs: David Stirling's mercenary operation in the North Yemen Civil War

stops.name: Washington, the Lockheed commissions
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1970 to 1975 span; pinned to the opening year
stops.campa: Between 1970 and 1975 Lockheed pays him one hundred and six million dollars in commissions, on rates climbing from two and a half percent to fifteen, to place its aircraft with the Saudi government. The arrangement surfaces in the congressional bribery investigations of the mid-seventies and helps produce the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, a statute written in part around the shape of one man's fee. Lockheed's own vice president for international marketing describes plainly what the company thought it had bought.
stops.quote: became for all practical purposes a marketing arm of Lockheed. Adnan would provide not only an entree but strategy, constant advice, and analysis.
stops.quote_source: Max Helzel, then vice president of Lockheed's international marketing, quoted in Richard Stengel, 'Businessman Adnan Khashoggi's High-Flying Realm,' Time, 19 January 1987
suggested_refs: The Church Committee hearings on Lockheed's foreign payments

stops.name: Long Beach, the Edgington Oil refinery
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the holding is listed without dates
stops.campa: Triad's American limb includes the Edgington Oil refinery at Long Beach, reported at some two hundred and fifty million dollars a year in revenue. The commissions have become capital and the capital has become plant: tanks, pipes, a workforce, a physical thing that burns and refines. He is no longer only a man taking a percentage of other men's contracts. He owns a stretch of the California coast, and the refinery ships a product a customer can hold in a hand.
suggested_refs: The Edgington Oil refinery at Long Beach, Triad's largest American industrial asset

stops.name: Washington, the Nixon campaign figure
stops.date_confidence: contested; the figure itself is arithmetically impossible
stops.campa: The claim recorded in the encyclopedia is that he gives two hundred million dollars to Richard Nixon's re-election campaign through a friendly bank, to buy standing with the administration. The figure cannot be true. Nixon's entire 1972 effort, the most expensive campaign in American history to that date, raised roughly sixty million dollars, and contributions from foreign nationals were illegal. The figure usually reported for Khashoggi is one million. The larger number is recorded here as a claim and not as a fact.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Adnan Khashoggi' (figure as stated there, uncorroborated)
suggested_refs: The 1972 Committee for the Re-Election of the President and its receipts

stops.name: Houston, the Galleria in the holdings list
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the holding is listed without dates
stops.campa: The Houston Galleria appears in the inventory of his American holdings, a shopping and office complex in the capital of the Texas oil business. The inventory is bare, a list without figures, and the two hundred and fifty million dollars often attached to his Texas real estate belongs in fact to the Long Beach refinery's annual revenue; the two facts have been merged in the retelling and are separated here. What the record supports is presence, not price: his name on Houston property in the boom decade.
suggested_refs: The Houston Galleria complex, one line in an unfigured inventory

stops.name: Paris, the prince of the bakchich
stops.date_confidence: attested to the publication date of the reproduced interview
stops.campa: A French journalist puts the nickname to him plainly, and he answers by naming the numbers: a hundred and six million from Lockheed, forty-five from Northrop, and the observation that he works independently, as an estate agent does. He is not embarrassed by the commissions. He considers them a profession, and asks what a lawyer or a doctor is for. In Paris he moves among the same arms ministries that spend the decade negotiating France's nuclear reactor deal with Iraq, a trade he has no documented hand in.
stops.quote: On vous appelle le "prince du bakchich".
stops.quote_source: Question put to Khashoggi in a Le Point interview, reproduced in La Revue du Liban et de l'Orient arabe, 19 February 1977, p. 33
sources: Le Point interview, 1977, via La Revue du Liban et de l'Orient arabe, 19 February 1977, p. 33
suggested_refs: The 1977 Le Point interview, the fullest first-person statement of his commission logic

segments.name: The Court in a Dozen Cities

stops.name: Beirut, the residence and the American friend
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the residence is listed without dates
stops.campa: Beirut is a residence in the years when the city is still the banking and brokerage crossroads of the Middle East, before its own war closes it. Here and in the cities like it he cultivates the Americans who matter, among them Miles Copeland, the intelligence officer who helped run the agency's Middle Eastern operations and who would still be describing their first meeting three decades later. No business is discussed at that meeting. That is the whole point of the meeting, and Copeland understood it.
stops.quote: Readers who've read in the Sunday papers about Adnan's jetset lifestyle will forgive me if I refrain from reporting details, and will only say that the meeting, no business discussed, put the two of us on a "Miles-and-Adnan" basis that has lasted for more than twenty years of business, parties and a very special kind of political action.
stops.quote_source: Miles Copeland, The Game Player (1989), p. 231, as quoted in the citation field of the English Wikipedia article; the memoir text itself was not independently located
sources: Miles Copeland, The Game Player (1989) (not independently verified)
suggested_refs: Miles Copeland's memoir The Game Player, the only source for the phrase

stops.name: New York, the penthouse at Olympic Tower
stops.date_confidence: attested; held from 1976 to 1993
stops.campa: He buys a penthouse duplex at Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue and keeps it from 1976 to 1993: its own swimming pool, five bedrooms, six bathrooms, indoor gardens, a ballroom, a sauna, and a catering kitchen built to serve three hundred seated guests. The residential entrance is at 641 Fifth Avenue; 645 is the office address. The apartment is not a home but an instrument, sized for the number of people he intends to have in one room at once. Anne Hathaway will live in the same unit until 2012.
suggested_refs: The Olympic Tower penthouse duplex, 641 Fifth Avenue

stops.name: Cannes, the Riviera circuit
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the residence is listed without dates
stops.campa: Cannes anchors the Riviera circuit: a residence, a mooring, a film festival that supplies the guest list. The coast between Cannes and Marbella becomes the physical form of the business, a chain of houses and berths in which introductions are made under no jurisdiction in particular. The press begins calling him the Onassis of the Arab world, and later the Great Gatsby of the Middle East. Neither epithet has been traced to a first author. Both are repeated until repetition does the work of description.
stops.quote_source: Recurring press characterization cited on the English Wikipedia article; original coiner and exact primary wording untraced, carried as reconstruction
sources: Euro Weekly News obituary, 12 June 2017 (for the epithet)
suggested_refs: The Cannes moorings and the press epithets attached to them

stops.name: Rome, the second marriage and the third
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1978 marriage; the Rome placement is inferred
stops.campa: A Rome residence joins the European chain. He marries Laura Biancolini, Italian-born, who takes the name Lamia, four years after divorcing Soraya. The same record that dates this marriage from 1978 also records a third: Shahpari Azam Zanganeh, married 1991 and divorced 2014, overlapping the Lamia marriage entirely. Accounts describing the second marriage as lasting undisturbed until his death are omitting the third, which sits in the same infobox they are reading. The contradiction is left standing.
suggested_refs: The overlapping marriage records of 1978, 1991 and 2014

stops.name: Viareggio, Benetti delivers the Nabila
stops.date_confidence: attested to the delivery year
stops.campa: The Benetti yard at Viareggio delivers the Nabila, eighty-five and a half meters, at the time the largest privately owned yacht in the world, named for his daughter. Some accounts place the build in France; the yard is Italian, the delivery year is 1980, and the source usually cited for the France claim states no build location at all. He is not a merchant with a boat. The Nabila is territory of its own, moored outside every jurisdiction that would otherwise have to record who came aboard.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Trump Princess' (the yacht under its later names)
suggested_refs: The Benetti yard at Viareggio and the yacht later renamed Trump Princess and Kingdom 5KR

stops.name: Acapulco, Las Brisas among the holdings
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the holding is listed without dates
stops.campa: Las Brisas at Acapulco appears among the Latin American resort holdings, a hillside of pink jeeps and private pools above the Pacific. The listing is bare and unfigured, one line in an inventory, and is carried here as reconstruction rather than record. The holdings map shows accommodation on every continent, each house standing well away from the country whose contract is being discussed inside it. Mexico in these years asks the fewest questions of an arriving guest.
suggested_refs: Las Brisas, Acapulco, one line in the Triad holdings list

stops.name: Nairobi, the gateway to the Kenyan land
stops.date_confidence: inferred; no fetched source documents the stopover
stops.campa: Nairobi is the gateway to the Kenyan land, the runway and the city where the private aircraft come down before the run north. No fetched source documents the stopover; it is inference from the geography of the ranch he owns, and is flagged as inference. The Gulf money that buys African land in these decades usually arrives exactly this way, through a capital with good runways and few questions, and departs the same afternoon for a property that no road reaches quickly.
sources: Inferred stopover for the Laikipia property; not documented in fetched sources
suggested_refs: Nairobi's private aviation terminals in the 1980s

stops.name: Marbella, the Baraka estate
stops.date_confidence: attested for the period; the coordinate is an inland placement
stops.campa: On the hills above the Costa del Sol he builds Baraka, seven villas on an estate whose size the sources cannot agree on: the prose of one account calls it a thirteen-hundred-acre hunting preserve, while a news passage quoted in the same account calls it a five-thousand-acre spread. At the height of his fortune he is reported to spend as much as a quarter of a million dollars a day here. The parties are the product. Marbella's reputation as the coast where oil money meets arms money is partly his construction.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Adnan Khashoggi' (prose and block quotation, mutually contradictory on acreage)
suggested_refs: The Baraka estate above Puerto Banus, Marbella

stops.name: Laikipia, the ranch on the equator
stops.date_confidence: attested as ownership; the year is inferred
stops.campa: On the equator west of Nanyuki, between the Aberdare range and Mount Kenya, he owns a ranch: cattle country and game country at once, at the latitude where the year has no seasons. The land will pass through later owners and be reorganized as the Ol Pejeta Conservancy, which now holds the last northern white rhinos on earth. An arms broker's private savannah becomes, by a route nobody planned and nobody would have proposed, one of the more consequential pieces of conservation land in Africa.
suggested_refs: The Ol Pejeta Conservancy, Laikipia County, and its record of prior owners

stops.name: Paris, the French contracts close
stops.date_confidence: attested to the account published in 2005 about 1984
stops.campa: The French arms channel closes. Samir Traboulsi, the Lebanese intermediary who takes his place in the Paris deals, will be quoted two decades later on what he told Khashoggi at the moment of the break. Khashoggi's answer, given to the same newspaper, denies the story outright: the French never used a single intermediary, he says, they multiplied their channels, and Traboulsi owes him his first contract. Both versions are printed here and neither is adjudicated. After 1984 the Paris contracts no longer pass through him.
stops.quote: Tu dois cesser de polluer les contrats francais.
stops.quote_source: Samir Traboulsi to Khashoggi, as reported in Le Monde, 30 April 2005, 'Le carnet d'or de Samir Traboulsi'
sources: Le Monde, 30 April 2005, 'Le carnet d'or de Samir Traboulsi'
suggested_refs: The 2005 Le Monde account of the 1984 falling-out, printing both men's versions

stops.name: Salt Lake City, ground broken at the Triad Center
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the first of June 1982 his brother Essam, chairman of Triad America, breaks ground in downtown Salt Lake City on twenty-six acres: twin forty-story office towers, three residential towers of twenty-five stories, a hotel. The single tower actually begun, 1 Triad Center, is thirty-five stories, and construction halts after excavation and steel delivery. Broadcast House opens in July 1984. A Saudi arms broker's money is pouring concrete in the capital city of the Latter-day Saints.
suggested_refs: The Triad Center at 95 North 300 West, Salt Lake City

stops.name: Washington, a seat on the American University board
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He is seated on the board of trustees of American University in Washington, a Gulf fortune installed in the governance of an American campus a few miles from the agencies whose contracts made it. The trusteeship is the respectable end of the same instrument as the yacht and the estate: proximity, purchased and displayed. The seat holds for six years and ends in the same season that a United States attorney in Manhattan puts his name into a federal indictment.
suggested_refs: The American University board of trustees roster, 1983 to 1989

stops.name: Salt Lake City, the Utah Jazz in the inventory
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the claim rests on one holdings list and is contradicted elsewhere
stops.campa: The Utah Jazz appear in the inventory of Triad's holdings, an American basketball franchise on a list otherwise made of refineries and banks. The team's own record does not mention him: it names Sam Battistone's group as owner from 1979, with Larry H. Miller buying half in April 1985 and the remainder in 1986. The claim rests on one side's list alone and is carried as reconstruction. In these years the team plays at the Salt Palace; the Delta Center will not open until the 1991 season.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Utah Jazz' (which does not mention him)
suggested_refs: The Salt Palace, home of the Utah Jazz through the 1980s

stops.name: Khartoum, the airlift he may or may not have funded
stops.date_confidence: contested; the two records flatly disagree
stops.campa: Some accounts credit him with organizing and funding a covert airlift of Ethiopian Jews out of the Sudanese refugee camps to Israel, the operation known as Operation Moses. The account of the operation itself names the Israeli Defense Forces, the CIA, Mossad and Sudanese security services, and does not mention him anywhere. The contradiction between the two records is total and is left standing. What is not in doubt is that Khartoum in this season is a city where arrangements of exactly this kind are made.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Operation Moses' (which does not mention him)
suggested_refs: The Operation Moses airlift, November 1984 to January 1985

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the bridge money
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the routing is not confirmed in fetched sources
stops.campa: Israeli procurement channels move American weapons toward Iran, and the money that has to move ahead of the weapons cannot come from a government. This is the function Khashoggi performs. He is not the shipper and not the buyer; he is the bridge, advancing his own funds so that a transaction no state will admit to can be settled before any state has admitted to it. The specific Tel Aviv routing is not confirmed in the sources fetched and is carried as reconstruction, not as record.
sources: General historical record of the Iran-Contra affair; not confirmed in fetched sources
suggested_refs: The Israeli leg of the 1985 arms transfers to Iran

stops.name: Tehran, the far end of the pipeline
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the routing detail is not confirmed in fetched sources
stops.campa: At the far end of the pipeline is the Islamic Republic, at war with Iraq, embargoed, and holding American hostages in Lebanon through its proxies. Ayatollah Khomeini's government buys American missiles from the same government enforcing the embargo against it, paying prices inflated by exactly the risk of getting caught. Khashoggi is the hinge that makes the transaction payable, the middleman standing between an arms embargo and a buyer nobody in Washington will admit to selling to, advancing credit so the weapons can move before anyone signs a paper a court could later read.
suggested_refs: The 1985 to 1986 arms-for-hostages shipments to Tehran

stops.name: Hamburg, the meetings around Ghorbanifar
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed for the meetings; attested for the December interview
stops.campa: Hamburg is named in accounts of the arms pipeline as a meeting point for the network around Manucher Ghorbanifar, the former SAVAK agent who is the other of the two key middlemen. In a December 1985 interview Khashoggi states that Ghorbanifar had been head of European intelligence under the Iranian prime minister Mir-Hossein Mousavi. The interview is attested. The Hamburg meetings are not confirmed in the sources fetched and are carried as reconstruction.
sources: Tower Commission-era press accounts (not confirmed in fetched sources)
suggested_refs: Manucher Ghorbanifar's European movements, 1985 to 1986

stops.name: London, the loans and the bank
stops.date_confidence: contested; the same claim is tagged attested and reconstruction in the same research
stops.campa: He borrows to finance the Iran shipments, reportedly through the Bank of Credit and Commerce International, Agha Hasan Abedi's bank, with Saudi and American backing. The claim is unstable: the account of BCCI itself never mentions him once. One pass of the research tags the identical sentence attested; another calls it reconstruction, and the lower confidence is taken here. Mark Lombardi will later draw this network as arcs and nodes, and Khashoggi is a labeled node inside the drawing.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International' (which does not mention him)
suggested_refs: Mark Lombardi, 'BCCI-ICIC-FAB, 1972-91,' in which Khashoggi appears as a labeled node

stops.name: Washington, interviewed by the Tower Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested to the report's delivery; the interviews run from late 1986
stops.campa: The Tower Commission interviews eighty witnesses to the scheme, President Reagan among them, and Ghorbanifar, and Khashoggi. He is interviewed and not called to testify, and the eighty interviews are separate proceedings; accounts placing the three men in one room have compressed a list into a scene. The report is delivered on the twenty-sixth of February 1987. Officials of the United States government are prosecuted over this affair. Khashoggi's name appears in no indictment arising from it.
suggested_refs: The Tower Commission report, delivered 26 February 1987

stops.name: Bern, the Swiss arrest
stops.date_confidence: contested in both year and city; no article names the canton
stops.campa: Swiss authorities arrest him on charges of concealing funds tied to Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos, and hold him three months before reducing the case to obstruction of justice and mail fraud. Neither the city nor the year is firm. The sources say 1988, while the sequence of the American proceedings, an October 1988 indictment and a trial ending in July 1990, points toward 1989, and no article names a canton. Bern is a placement and is flagged as one. The arrest itself is not in doubt.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Adnan Khashoggi' (year only; no city given)
suggested_refs: Swiss federal records of the 1988 or 1989 detention and its reduced charges

stops.name: New York, indicted with the Marcoses
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A Manhattan federal grand jury indicts Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos together with eight associates, Khashoggi among them, on racketeering, conspiracy, fraud and obstruction of justice: some one hundred and three million dollars taken from the Philippine treasury and turned into Manhattan real estate and art. The indictment describes him as a Saudi Arabian businessman and weapons smuggler believed to have been involved with her husband's regime. That is the phrase the record keeps.
stops.quote: a Saudi Arabian businessman and weapons smuggler believed to have been involved with her husband's regime
stops.quote_source: Description of Khashoggi in the October 1988 Manhattan federal indictment, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Imelda Marcos'
suggested_refs: The October 1988 Manhattan federal indictment of Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos and eight associates

stops.name: Washington, the trusteeship resigned
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Formally indicted in the United States, he resigns his seat on the board of trustees of American University, ending six years of an arms broker's presence in the governance of a Washington campus. The university's problem is solved by a signature. His is not. For thirty years he has borrowed the reputations of other men and paid for the loan in commissions and hospitality. The borrowing runs in both directions, and in this season the lenders begin calling it in.
suggested_refs: American University trustee minutes for May 1989

stops.name: London, Queen record Khashoggi's Ship
stops.date_confidence: attested to the album release date
stops.campa: Queen release The Miracle, and one track on it is called Khashoggi's Ship. The song is about the Nabila and about nothing else, a shorthand for a party that cannot be stopped. He is under indictment in a New York federal court in the same month the record reaches the shops, and he no longer owns the yacht. No contract of his is remembered. What survives him in the widest circulation is four minutes of hard rock, named after a boat named after his daughter.
suggested_refs: Queen, 'Khashoggi's Ship,' on The Miracle, released 22 May 1989

stops.name: Foley Square, acquitted on all counts
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: After a three-month trial a federal jury in Manhattan acquits Khashoggi and Imelda Marcos of all racketeering and fraud charges. He is not convicted. The fortune is gone regardless: the same season reports his net worth at some eight million dollars, down from an estimated four billion at the start of the decade. The acquittal restores his liberty and nothing else. The verdict is unambiguous in the record, and any account calling his personal outcome unresolved has not read the sentence that states it.
suggested_refs: The July 1990 verdict of the United States District Court, Southern District of New York

stops.name: Paris, the Alma tunnel and the nephew
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: His sister Samira married Mohamed Al-Fayed in 1954; their only child, Dodi Fayed, dies in the Alma tunnel with Diana, Princess of Wales. Khashoggi is the uncle of a man at the center of the most mythologized death of the century's end, and the surname enters a conspiracy literature he had no hand in building. The same Paris ground that once held his arms-ministry meetings now holds this too, one tunnel below the same river, thirteen years after his contracts closed here.
suggested_refs: The Pont de l'Alma underpass, 31 August 1997

stops.name: Marseille, lunch with Richard Perle
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He meets Richard Perle, former United States Assistant Secretary of Defense and then chairman of the Defense Policy Board, to discuss the prospects of Perle's venture fund with the Saudi government. Seymour Hersh publishes the meeting and Perle's conflicts of interest become a public question. Khashoggi is sixty-seven and has been out of the money for a decade, and he can still produce a serving Pentagon adviser at a lunch table on the French coast. The logic he offers Hersh is the logic of 1963.
stops.quote: If there is no war, why is there a need for security? If there is a war, of course, billions of dollars will have to be spent.
stops.quote_source: Khashoggi to Seymour Hersh, 'Lunch With The Chairman,' The New Yorker, 17 March 2003
sources: Seymour Hersh, 'Lunch With The Chairman,' The New Yorker, 17 March 2003 (seen via the English Wikipedia article; newyorker.com refused direct fetch)
suggested_refs: Seymour Hersh, 'Lunch With The Chairman,' The New Yorker, 17 March 2003

stops.name: Salt Lake City, the tower passes to the Church
stops.date_confidence: attested for the sale; the tenancy dates run to 2017
stops.campa: The unfinished Triad Center is sold by M and S Triad Center to Zions Securities, and passes into the property of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints through its Deseret Management Corporation. Broadcast House, the ten-story North Plaza building and the parking structure now hold KSL-TV, KSL Radio, Ensign College, the BYU Salt Lake Center and the Deseret News; BYU-Pathway Worldwide moves its headquarters in during August 2017. Utah's tallest building was never built.

stops.name: Van Nuys, the last case
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The Securities and Exchange Commission sues him for securities fraud in connection with Genesis Intermedia, a Los Angeles company at the tail end of the dot-com stock promotion era. The case is dismissed two years later, with neither an admission nor a denial of the allegations. It is the last legal proceeding of his life, and it ends the way most of them ended, with no finding entered against him and nothing placed on the record about what took place inside the company.
suggested_refs: SEC v. Khashoggi, filed 2006, dismissed 2008

stops.name: London, death at St Thomas' Hospital
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He dies at St Thomas' Hospital on the Thames, opposite the Palace of Westminster, aged eighty-one, under treatment for Parkinson's disease. No burial place is recorded in any reachable source. A Find a Grave memorial exists under the number 180710080, but the site refused every request with an HTTP 403 and the cemetery field could not be read. The man who kept houses in a dozen cities has no attested grave in any of them. The gap is stated here as a gap and not filled.
suggested_refs: St Thomas' Hospital, Lambeth; and the unresolved burial record

stops.name: Istanbul, the consulate and the nephew
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Sixteen months after his death his nephew Jamal Khashoggi, a journalist, is killed inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, and the surname returns to the front pages attached to the opposite thing: not the sale of weapons to a state but the killing of a critic by one. No accessible source records how much contact the two men had, and that is left as a gap. One family produced, in two generations, the century's most famous arms broker and its most famous murdered reporter.
suggested_refs: The Saudi consulate on Istanbul's Beyoglu side, 2 October 2018
